comments.content: Perhaps we could check [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/blob/development/src/handlers/payout/action.ts#L75) that if an author of a comment is the `ubiquibot` and comment contains `https://pay.ubq.fi?claim=` then we could consider it to be a "bot posted claim URL" event

Check this [issue](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/643)
There are 2 permits generated for different networks:
1. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/643#issuecomment-1569384273
2. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/643#issuecomment-1607152588
What happened:
1. When the issue was closed the 1st time  the payout network was set to ethereum mainnet so the bot generated the [1st permit](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/643#issuecomment-1569384273)
2. Then we updated the bot's config and switched to gnosis chain for payouts
3. When issue was closed the 2nd time the bot [couldn't find](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/blob/development/src/handlers/payout/action.ts#L75) the permit URL for gnosis chain so generated a new permit
So on step 3 the bot should have been looking for permit for any chain, not the currently set in the config.

Yes, parsing the URL with `URLSearchParams` is a better approach
This PR solves the original issue + we don't have plans of adding more query params besides `claim` and `network` so I don't think that refactoring to `URLSearchParams` is an urgent issue
No, the generated URL is `https://pay.ubq.fi?claim=` so everything is fine
